name: Boston
title: Holidays in Boston
intro: Follow a red line through history, see whales off the coast and catch a ball game. Here's what Boston is like with the family and when to go.
facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and October are best, and October brings New England's famous autumn colours. Summer is warm and lively. Winter is cold and snowy.

things.name: Freedom Trail
things.blurb: Follow the red line on the pavement past 16 historic sites.

things.name: Boston Tea Party Ships
things.blurb: Throw tea into the harbour like the colonists did.

things.name: New England Aquarium
things.blurb: A giant ocean tank, penguins and sea turtles.

things.name: Museum of Science
things.blurb: A big hands-on museum with a lightning show.

things.name: Swan boats
things.blurb: A gentle pedal boat ride in the Public Garden, from spring to late summer.

things.name: Whale watching
things.blurb: Boats leave the harbour from spring to autumn to see humpbacks.

faqs.question: Is Boston good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's walkable, historic and feels a bit British, which makes it an easy first US city. Children love the tea party and the swan boats.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Four or five nights, or add Cape Cod or a New England road trip.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: Most British passport holders, children included, apply for an ESTA online before they fly rather than a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Is there a direct flight?
faqs.answer: Yes, from London Heathrow in about seven hours.
